newsItems.headline: Traders see September rate hike as European Central Bank mulls energy price spike
Dollar hits new 40-year high versus yen, euro softer after ECB stands pat on rates - Reuters

briefing.briefing: Right now, the most important forces shaping gold are a resilient US dollar, rising bond yields [the interest rate governments pay on their debt — higher yields make gold less attractive because gold pays no interest], and a market that has already moved more than its average daily range. The dollar index (DXY) sits at 101.44 and the yen has weakened dramatically, which about 19 hours ago Reuters confirmed with a headline about the dollar hitting a 40-year high against the yen — a strong dollar typically pushes gold prices lower, all else equal. About 7 hours ago, CNBC reported that traders are pricing in a September rate hike from the European Central Bank due to an energy price spike; a more hawkish ECB [a central bank leaning toward raising rates, not cutting them] supports a stronger euro but also signals a global tightening mood that can weigh on risk assets and commodities including gold. Despite this, gold is still trading at a remarkable $4,049, so the underlying demand story hasn't collapsed — geopolitical risk (GPR at 173.6, which is elevated) and a high open interest reading suggest institutional players are still active in the market. Real yields [bond yields after stripping out inflation] are high at 2.39%, which is historically a headwind for gold. Directional bias leans mildly BEARISH from here, mostly because today's ADR [Average Daily Range — how far gold typically moves in a day] of $86.50 has already been exceeded by $100.80, meaning gold has moved MORE than its typical daily distance — this dramatically reduces the probability of a clean, low-risk trend-following trade developing in the remaining hours. There is no scheduled economic news today according to the calendar, and no high-impact events flagged for later this week, which removes one source of volatility but also removes a catalyst that could restart momentum. Fed expectations show a 96% chance of no rate change at the July 29th meeting, so that is unlikely to surprise markets. Confidence in this mild bearish lean is 4/10 — the lack of a fresh catalyst and the already-exhausted daily range make any directional conviction low; if price pulls back to a clear support level [a price zone where buyers have previously stepped in] and forms a buying signal on the 5-minute chart, a short-term long [a buy trade] could still work within the broader uptrend, but position size [the amount of money risked per trade] should be small given how extended the move already is. For trend-following trades using ICT methodology tonight, patience is your edge — wait for price to reset into a discount zone [a price level well below recent highs] before looking for bullish signals, and keep risk tight. Screenshot this: when gold has already moved past its average daily range, the smartest trade is often no trade — wait for tomorrow's fresh range.
